_comment: Pinned Piper voice per actor type. NEVER change one of these after scenarios exist: a voice is the only cue distinguishing one actor from another, so swapping one silently invalidates every provenance question in the bank. Adding a voice requires regenerating the bank.

security.why: Northern English male. The most immediately identifiable accent in the set — Security speaks in every phase and during the finale, so it must never be mistaken for anyone else.

construction.why: Lower-pitched American male. Reads as a working crew voice and sits well away from the other two males in both accent and pitch.

cargo.why: Sri Lankan-accented English male. Third male voice, distinct from the other two by accent rather than pitch, which is a stronger cue than pitch alone.

medical.why: British RP female, high quality. Calm and precise, which suits Medical, and the only 'high' model among the human actors.

civilian.why: Scottish female. Chosen over a second American female specifically to keep it unmistakable from Medical and from the system voice.

system.why: The flattest, most neutral model available — appropriate for automated station announcements. Always rendered through the PA filter below, so it can never be confused with a person.

pa_intercom.purpose: Make automated station announcements instantly recognisable as machine-spoken. Without this the system voice is just a seventh person, and provenance questions about who said what get muddier.
pa_intercom.note: Band-limits to telephone/intercom range and compresses hard. Applied at generation time only; the runtime plays the rendered file as-is.

distinctness_matrix._comment: The weakest pair is what determines whether provenance is answerable. Reviewed pairwise at pinning time.
distinctness_matrix.sexes: 3 male (security, construction, cargo), 3 female (medical, civilian, system)
distinctness_matrix.accents: Northern English, American, Sri Lankan English, British RP, Scottish, American-neutral
distinctness_matrix.weakest_pair: medical (British RP female) vs civilian (Scottish female) — same sex and both British, separated by a strong regional accent difference
distinctness_matrix.system_separation: system is additionally separated from all five human voices by the pa_intercom filter

rejected.en_US-amy-medium: American female — too close to en_US-lessac-high, which is reserved for the system voice
rejected.en_US-libritts-high: 904-speaker multi-speaker model; speaker selection is not stable enough to pin
rejected.en_US-danny-low: low quality; radio messages are audio-only with no transcript, so intelligibility is not optional
